content.thinking:
I'm working out the postmortem's symptom and causal chain: account pages failed for shoppers from the start, with the io-pay card lookup returning 503 as the likely cause.

I'm ruling out production changes for the causal chain: there were no deploys or flag changes in the window, so the trigger looks like io-pay itself failing. I'm leaving out the earlier ClientDisconnected errors, since they stopped before onset and look like baseline noise.

I'm checking whether the root cause holds up: io-shop failed the whole account page on io-pay's 503 instead of rendering without card details, but the evidence doesn't show why io-pay failed in the first place.

I'm checking whether io-pay's failure is what took down io-shop: the account page request fails when the card lookup errors, which Gbf7d shows. The deeper reason io-pay started returning 503s is still unknown, but the mechanism on the io-shop side is supported by the log. Next I'm drafting the contributing factors, starting with the missing fallback when the card lookup fails.

I'm sketching the root cause and the contributing factors now: the card lookup failing with a 503 and io-shop failing the whole request, plus the missing fallback and the alert that never reached on-call.

I'm adding a second contributing factor: nobody was paged when the alert fired, because the alert routing never reached on-call. Had it been wired to page on-call, someone would have been pulled in to contact IO Payments Ltd right away instead of the incident escalating unnoticed. I'm also planning the action item to render account pages without card details when the io-pay lookup fails.

I'm drafting the action items now: one to add a test confirming account pages render when io-pay returns 503, and one to route the io-shop high error rate alert to on-call paging.

I'm noting the remaining lessons: the investigator placed the start at T6, and the io-pay link formed as a candidate at T13. Argus checked the flag history at T15 and correctly refused a change at T17, escalating instead. For the still-at-risk section, account pages could keep failing while io-pay returns errors, and a later io-pay outage could break them again. I'm also listing the assumptions: that the io-pay 503s account for the failures, and that the logged counts stand in for the broader traffic, since the io-pay service itself wasn't checked directly.

I'm writing up the plain-language cause and the causal chain now: the payment provider's card lookup began returning 503s, and account page requests failed whenever that lookup failed. I'm ruling out io-shop deploys and flag changes for the day before onset, since none show up in that window.

I'm laying out the third causal step: io-pay, run by IO Payments Ltd, began returning 503s at onset, and the record doesn't show why since its state is outside what I can read.

I'm noting the lessons that went well: the Investigator placed the incident's start at T6 from the metrics, and traced the failing account page requests to io-pay's card lookup errors in io-shop's logs by T13. Argus then checked the flag history at T15 and found no flag change by anyone else.

I'm noting that the Investigator's "went well" entry at T17 is the point where Argus declined to act on another company's service and escalated, and I'll record that escalation as a separate item.

action_items.item: Make the io-shop account page render without card details, instead of failing the request, when io-pay's card lookup returns an error.
Add a test that the account page still renders when io-pay's card lookup returns {Gbf7d.1}.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages failed to load. io-shop's own log reported that the account page error rate was at its worst, and from the onset account page requests failed.

ruled_out.what: A deploy, release or flag change to io-shop: no production changes came back for the day before the onset.
A flag change by anyone other than Argus: the flag provider's history showed none in the hour it read.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed because the card lookup that io-shop makes to the third-party payment provider io-pay returned {Gbf7d.1}. io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 and failed the request.
io-pay, which IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning {Gbf7d.1} on the card lookup at the onset. The record does not show why: io-pay's own state was not read, only io-shop's logs of its replies.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card started rejecting those requests, and the shop's account pages failed every time that request failed.

contributing_factors.factor: When io-pay's card lookup failed, io-shop failed the whole account page request. No fallback was seen, such as rendering the page without the card details or using a cached copy.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages would have loaded without card details while io-pay was failing, so most shoppers would have seen a page that still worked instead of an error.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been engaged when the alert fired and could have asked IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay sooner, which would have shortened the outage.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident from the service's per-minute metrics.
The Investigator Agent traced the failing account page requests to io-pay's card lookup errors in io-shop's own logs.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag change by anyone else.
Argus declined to act on a failure in a service another company runs, and recorded the request to IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay.
Argus escalated the incident instead of leaving it open with no mitigation.

input.root_cause: Account page requests in io-shop call the card lookup of io-pay, a payment provider run by IO Payments Ltd. From the onset io-pay answered that lookup with {Gbf7d.1}, and io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed and failed the whole account page request.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps rejecting the card lookup, and could fail the same way the next time io-pay has trouble.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
